findings.title: Spy restore is not guaranteed if the assertion fails
findings.body: `selection.mockRestore()` runs after `expect(box).toBeChecked()` at line 373. If that assertion throws, the `getSelection` mock stays installed for the rest of the file, and later tests would fail for an unrelated reason. Restore it in `afterEach` or in a `try/finally`. The `afterEach` in this file's `vitest` import is already available.

contracts.action: Click on a selectable finding row now skips the toggle when the page has a non-empty text selection
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing row onClick in the same handler, which toggles via setFixing unless the target is inside an input
contracts.before_after: Before: any non-input click toggled the row, including the click that ends a drag-select over a file name. After: a click with non-empty window.getSelection() returns early and does not toggle. The input-target check at line 214 still runs first, so the checkbox's own onChange toggles only once.
contracts.visible_effect: Dragging over a name to copy it no longer unticks the row. A plain click collapses any prior selection on mousedown, so a normal click still toggles.
contracts.failure_mode: window.getSelection() can return null; optional chaining makes that fall through to the toggle. No async work, so there is no rejection or timeout path.

It runs after the input-target check, so the checkbox still toggles once. The test mocks a selection, clicks the row, and asserts the box keeps its state.
